symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of a source vector.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of a target vector, with s < t and gcd(s,t) = 1.
symbols.quote: Here $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width parameter
symbols.meaning: The integer width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The integer $\alpha$ is the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.

symbols.name: normalized Fourier transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length s.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$, and $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: normalized Fourier transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length t.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$, and $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: source coordinate permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-s vectors given by (P_s u)_j = u_{tj}.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$, and $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: target coordinate permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-t vectors given by (P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$, and $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: source-to-target contraction
symbols.meaning: A linear contraction from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: $A$ is a linear contraction from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$, and $B_0$ is a linear contraction from vectors of length $t$ to vectors of length $s$.

symbols.name: target-to-source contraction
symbols.meaning: A linear contraction from vectors of length t to vectors of length s.
symbols.quote: $A$ is a linear contraction from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$, and $B_0$ is a linear contraction from vectors of length $t$ to vectors of length $s$.

symbols.name: Gaussian map S
symbols.meaning: A Gaussian-weighted map from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

symbols.name: Gaussian map T
symbols.meaning: A Gaussian-weighted map from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

symbols.name: Gaussian diagonal map
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on length-s vectors that multiplies coordinate j by a Gaussian factor.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $j$ by a Gaussian factor, and $C$ selects from a length-$t$ vector the coordinates at the indices nearest $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.

symbols.name: coordinate selection map
symbols.meaning: The map that selects from a length-t vector the coordinates at the indices nearest tj/s, for each j.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $j$ by a Gaussian factor, and $C$ selects from a length-$t$ vector the coordinates at the indices nearest $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The map CTD, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Put $N=CTD$, a map close to the identity.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling is a technique that replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, which the integer multiplier needs.
Gaussian resampling computes the transforms of a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) from power-of-two transforms.
